events.system:
P = 4-(prop-2-yn-1-yl)benzaldehyde
P --[NaBH₄, C₂H₅OH]--> Q
Q --[SOCl₂, pyridine]--> R
R --[AgNO₂]--> S
R --[NaCN, DMSO]--> T
T --[HBr (2 equiv)]--> U
events.hidden_link: P has an aldehyde and an alkyne; NaBH4 selectively reduces only the aldehyde to alcohol (Q). SOCl2 converts the alcohol to a benzylic chloride (R). AgNO2 substitutes the chloride to give a nitroalkane (S), while NaCN yields a nitrile (T). Addition of 2 equivalents of HBr to the terminal alkyne in T follows Markovnikov's rule, forming a geminal dihalide (U).
events.route: 1. NaBH4 reduces the -CHO group of P to -CH2OH (Q), leaving the alkyne intact. 2. SOCl2 replaces -OH with -Cl (R). 3. AgNO2 reacts with the benzylic chloride via an SN1/SN2 pathway favoring the nitro compound (S) due to the silver ion's affinity for chloride, leaving the nitrogen to attack. 4. NaCN reacts via SN2 to give the nitrile (T). 5. HBr (2 equiv) adds to the terminal alkyne -CH2-C#CH via Markovnikov addition to yield the geminal dihalide -CH2-C(Br)2-CH3 (U).
events.student_must_notice: The ambident nucleophile chemistry: AgNO2 yields the nitro compound (S) whereas NaNO2/KNO2 would yield the nitrite; NaCN yields the nitrile (T) whereas AgCN would yield the isocyanide. Furthermore, the electrophilic addition of HBr to the alkyne follows Markovnikov's rule to give a geminal dihalide, not a vicinal or anti-Markovnikov product.
events.trap: Students may mistakenly predict S as an alkyl nitrite (-O-N=O) and T as an isocyanide (-NC) due to confusion over ambident nucleophiles. They might also predict anti-Markovnikov addition for U, expecting a 1,2-dibromide or 1,1-dibromide at the terminal carbon.
events.given: The reaction scheme with P named and reagents provided.
events.asked: Identify the correct statements regarding the functional groups, structures, and reaction products of S, T, and U.
events.why_hard: It requires mastery of ambident nucleophile regioselectivity (AgNO2 vs NaCN) and correct application of Markovnikov's rule for double hydrohalogenation of an alkyne, penalizing any confusion with plausible but incorrect structural isomers.

options.A: Compound S is a nitro compound, whereas compound T is an alkyl nitrile.
options.B: Compound U is a geminal dihalide with exactly 4 sp3 hybridized carbon atoms.
options.C: Complete reduction of T with LiAlH4 produces a secondary amine.
options.D: The conversion of R to S yields an alkyl nitrite as the major product.

members.working: P: p-(propargyl)benzaldehyde, Ar-CH2-C≡CH with CHO on ring. (1) NaBH4 reduces CHO to CH2OH → Q (4-propargylbenzyl alcohol). (2) SOCl2/pyridine converts OH to Cl → R = Ar-CH2-Cl (with propargyl chain intact). (3) R + AgNO2 gives the nitro compound S = Ar-CH2-NO2 → S contains a nitro group: (A) correct. (4) R + NaCN gives T = Ar-CH2-CN (SN2 on benzyl chloride) → nitrile present: (B) correct. (5) T + 2 equiv HBr: the terminal alkyne Ar-CH2-C≡CH adds HBr twice to give the gem-dibromide U = Ar-CH2-CBr2-CH3. Gem-dibromides have no multiple bond, so U does not decolourise bromine water: (C) false. sp3 carbons in U: benzylic CH2 (1), CBr2 carbon (2), terminal CH3 (3); ring carbons are sp2 → total 3, not 2: (D) false.
